answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make every identity earn trust through a public history of useful work. Like a tide that only rises after many waves, a new agent starts with near-zero weight: each verified task it completes adds a little reputation, and high-value trades need a long record built from dawn to dusk, not a fresh account. An attacker can spin up a thousand empty identities, but each one is an oasis with no water — no history, no trust, no volume. Faking that history costs real compute and time per identity, so flooding the market costs more than it can ever earn back.
